title: Fuzzy search with typo tolerance and ranking
when: Exact search is not enough: users misspell names, type abbreviations, or need ranked suggestions for autocomplete or a command palette.
prompt:
Goal: A small ranked fuzzy matcher that finds what users mean, highlights matched letters and stays fast.
Steps:
1. Normalize query and candidates the same way: lowercase, strip accent marks, collapse spaces; precompute once.
2. Score in tiers: exact, prefix, word starts (initials), subsequence, then typo tolerant.
3. Subsequence score rewards consecutive letters and matches after a space, dash or capital; penalizes gaps and late starts.
4. Typos: Damerau Levenshtein with early exit, 1 edit for words of 4 or more letters, 2 for 8 or more.
5. Rank by tier, score, shorter candidate, then recency; return the top 20.
6. Highlight matched ranges with text nodes and <mark> elements; above 10 thousand items prefilter by trigrams or first letter.
Quality bar:
- Common typos put the right item first in tests.
- Each keystroke ranks in under 16 ms on the target data.
- Highlights cover exactly the matched letters.
Pitfalls:
- Edit distance against everything on every keystroke without a length prefilter.
- Different normalization for score and highlight.
- Hundreds of weak matches returned.
Verify:
- [ ] A table of queries with expected first results.
- [ ] Highlight built from text nodes and mark.
- [ ] One shared normalize function.
- [ ] No innerHTML with data.
Output: js/fuzzy.js exporting search(items, query, { keys, limit }) and highlight(text, ranges), plus tests.

examples.input: search contacts even when I type "jhon" or "mra silva"
examples.output: tiered fuzzy search with typo tolerance ranking John and Maria Silva first, mark highlights
